stories.excerpt: Woodside Health, an Ohio-based private equity firm specializing in healthcare real estate, has completed the sale of Cornerstone Plaza, a medical and retail property located in the Dallas-Fort Worth metropolitan area. Built in 2002, the property is strategically positioned in Southlake, Texas, and the asset is anchored by Cook Children’s. In addition to its healthcare tenancy, the property includes several retail users. JLL arranged financing from Hillcrest Bank, a division of NBH Bank, on behalf of the borrower, Brownlee Waggoner Holdings. JLL Capital Market’s Debt Advisory team, representing the borrower, was led by Senior Managing Director John Rose, Director Kristi Leonard and Associate Chad Lisbeth. The retail center was originally built in 2002 and comprises 51,664 square feet of net rentable area across two buildings situated on 5.9 acres with 273 parking spaces. “Cornerstone Plaza is exceptionally well located within the Southlake market and supported by a quality tenant roster led by Cook Children’s,” said Ben Barr, Woodside Health Principal. The post ... appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Woodside Health sold Cornerstone Plaza, 51,664 SF medical/retail in Southlake, TX.
Cook Children's anchors property; JLL arranged Hillcrest Bank financing for buyer.
2002-built asset in DFW market with mixed healthcare and retail tenancy.
stories.summary: Woodside Health exited Cornerstone Plaza, a 51,664-square-foot medical and retail property in Southlake, Texas, anchored by Cook Children's. The two-building asset on 5.9 acres was built in 2002 and financed by Hillcrest Bank via JLL. The sale reflects continued healthcare-anchored retail velocity in the Dallas-Fort Worth corridor.
stories.impact: Limited direct signal. Healthcare-anchored retail in Southlake trades on different fundamentals than multifamily; no demand or supply implications for apartment development in DFW unless it signals broader tenant credit strength or market stability in the submarket.

stories.title: Bluhawk Announces Eight New Retail Tenants at Kansas MXU Center
stories.excerpt: Bluhawk, a 277-acre master-planned development in Overland Park, Kansas, announced a new lineup of tenants led by outdoor lifestyle brand L.L.Bean. The lineup includes L.L.Bean, Spavia Day Spa, JETSET Pilates, Chicken Salad Chick, Brookside Barkery & Bath, Amorino, Everbowl and Bruú Café, with additional tenants to come. “Bluhawk continues to attract best-in-class brands that reflect the project’s strength and the demand we are seeing from both consumers and retailers,” said Kent Price, president of Price Brothers, the developer and manager of Bluhawk. L.L.Bean’s arrival marks the brand’s return to Kansas City. Amorino, an Italian gelato brand, will make its Kansas City, Kansas, and Missouri debut at Bluhawk. Construction at the complex is progressing following the development’s 2025 groundbreaking, and J.Crew Factory, Buckle and Barnes & Noble are now open. The project celebrated a hospitality milestone with the May 2026 opening of Holiday Inn Express by IHG, developed and managed by Price Hospitality, and the first of three planned hotels. The post Bluhawk Announces Eight New Retail Tenants at Kansas MXU Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Bluhawk master-planned (277 acres, Overland Park, KS) signed 8 retail tenants including L.L.Bean.
Holiday Inn Express opens May 2026; three hotels planned at mixed-use development.
L.L.Bean returns to Kansas City market; Amorino makes KC debut at Bluhawk.
stories.summary: Bluhawk, a 277-acre mixed-use development in Overland Park, Kansas, announced eight new retail tenants led by L.L.Bean's return to Kansas City, plus Spavia Day Spa, JETSET Pilates, Chicken Salad Chick, and others. The first of three planned hotels—a Holiday Inn Express—opens May 2026. The project signals strong retail and hospitality demand in the Kansas City metro.
stories.impact: Mixed-use developments with strong retail/hospitality leasing velocity can indicate underlying job and population growth. Kansas City metro, particularly Johnson County, is seeing retail and hospitality confidence; this may signal demand tailwinds for multifamily in Overland Park and adjacent submarkets, though Bluhawk itself is likely master-planned mixed-use rather than a pure apartment play.

stories.title: Kidder Mathews Arranges Sale of Mixed-Use Apartments in WA
stories.excerpt: A nine-unit apartment complex in Wenatchee, Washington, has sold for $1.85 million. Kidder Mathews Vice President Max Frame of the Simon Anderson Multifamily Team, based at the firm’s Seattle headquarters, represented the seller.Located at 475 N. Elliott Avenue, the 6,444-square-foot property was built in 2015 and includes eight residential units and one commercial space. The turn-key building sits across the street from Wenatchee Valley College and within walking distance of downtown.The property went under contract after just six days on the market. The buyer submitted an all-cash offer with no financing contingency, completed a 10-day contingency period, and closed the transaction within 28 days. “The speed and certainty of this transaction demonstrate the strong demand for well-located, turn-key multifamily assets in Wenatchee,” said Frame. “The property’s proximity to Wenatchee Valley College and downtown, along with its mix of residential and commercial space, made it an especially compelling opportunity.” Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Gain firsthand insights from industry leaders on capital markets, development, operations, financing, and investment trends while expanding your network with the people making deals happen. See you on September 22! The post Kidder Mathews Arranges Sale of Mixed-Use Apartments in WA appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 9-unit apartment complex sold for $1.85M in Wenatchee, WA (6,444 SF, 2015-built).
Mixed-use with 8 residential units, 1 commercial space; all-cash offer within 6 days.
Location: across from Wenatchee Valley College, downtown walking distance.
stories.summary: A nine-unit mixed-use apartment complex at 475 N. Elliott Avenue in Wenatchee, Washington, sold for $1.85 million. Built in 2015, the 6,444-square-foot property includes eight residential units and one commercial space, positioned near Wenatchee Valley College. The all-cash offer closed within six days on market.
stories.impact: Minimal. Wenatchee small-asset transactions reflect local demand but lack scale or capital intensity relevant to major multifamily developers. Quick all-cash sale suggests buyer confidence but insufficient evidence of broader market supply/demand dynamics.

stories.title: Clear Investment Group Acquires 300-Unit DC Multifamily Property
stories.excerpt: Clear Investment Group, a Chicago-based real estate investment firm, has acquired Woodland Estates, a 300-unit multifamily community in Southeast Washington, D.C. The acquisition marks the firm’s second investment in the Washington metropolitan area, bringing its regional portfolio to nearly 1,000 apartment units.Woodland Estates was acquired through a receivership auction, creating a value-add opportunity for Clear Opportunities Fund II. Located in the Anacostia neighborhood, approximately five miles from downtown Washington, D.C., the property will undergo significant capital improvements to modernize the community. “The acquisition of Woodland Estates reflects exactly the type of opportunity we seek—well-located workforce housing that can be acquired at an exceptional basis and meaningfully improved for both residents and investors,” said Amy Rubenstein, CEO of Clear Investment Group. “Washington, D.C. continues to demonstrate resilient multifamily fundamentals driven by a diverse employment base, strong household incomes, and sustained demand for quality affordable housing. We are excited to expand our presence in this market.” The post Clear Investment Group Acquires 300-Unit DC Multifamily Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Clear Investment Group acquired 300-unit Woodland Estates in Southeast Washington, DC via receivership auction.
Property in Anacostia, ~5 miles from downtown DC; value-add capex opportunity.
Acquisition brings Clear's DC portfolio to nearly 1,000 units; reflects workforce housing demand.
stories.summary: Clear Investment Group, a Chicago-based firm, acquired Woodland Estates, a 300-unit multifamily property in Southeast Washington, D.C.'s Anacostia neighborhood, through a receivership auction. The acquisition brings Clear's regional portfolio to approximately 1,000 units and signals opportunity in workforce housing with capital-improvement potential. The firm cited resilient DC multifamily fundamentals driven by diverse employment, strong household incomes, and sustained affordable-housing demand.
stories.impact: Receivership/distressed acquisitions in DC indicate either prior-cycle mispricing or current operational stress, but Clear's comment on 'resilient multifamily fundamentals' and continued expansion suggests DC fundamentals remain solid. Anacostia—historically underserved—may be experiencing demand migration as downtown/core markets tighten; watch whether this signals emerging submarket appreciation and development pipeline opportunities in less-dense DC submarkets.

stories.title: Minority-Owned Construction Firm IMC Construction Expands to DC
stories.excerpt: IMC Construction, the largest minority-owned contractor in the country, is expanding into the DMV with the opening of a new regional hub in Bethesda, Maryland. IMC has recently started work with clients such as Merck and Charles River Laboratories, positioning it to contribute to similar developments in the D.C. region with the new regional team. The new office will be led by Dan Baker, Vice President; Pavlo Villhauer, Project Executive; and Debbie Jones, Business Development Manager. “The Washington metropolitan area represents a tremendous opportunity, but we knew our success would depend on having the right team in place from day one,” said Michael Lloyd, President and CEO of IMC Construction. The firm’s office will be located at 6903 Rockledge Drive in Bethesda. Building on the establishment of regional headquarters in New Jersey and Delaware, the Bethesda office will serve as a hub for clients throughout Washington, D.C., Maryland and Northern Virginia. The post Minority-Owned Construction Firm IMC Construction Expands to DC appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: IMC Construction (largest minority-owned US contractor) opens Bethesda, MD regional hub.
DMV expansion led by Dan Baker (VP), Pavlo Villhauer (Project Exec), Debbie Jones (BD).
New office to serve DC, Maryland, Northern Virginia after recent Merck, Charles River projects.
stories.summary: IMC Construction, the nation's largest minority-owned contractor, established a regional headquarters in Bethesda, Maryland, to serve Washington, D.C., Maryland, and Northern Virginia. The office will be led by Dan Baker, Pavlo Villhauer, and Debbie Jones, and follows recent work with Merck and Charles River Laboratories. The expansion builds on existing regional hubs in New Jersey and Delaware.
stories.impact: A major contractor entering/expanding in DC signals confidence in the development pipeline and capital availability. Increased construction capacity and competition in the DMV may pressure labor cost inflation but also improve execution timelines. For multifamily developers, this expands capacity for mid/large projects; monitor whether IMC's presence and client base (pharma, biotech) correlate with life sciences campus development that could drive secondary housing demand.

stories.title: Waste Management Buys 146-Acre Miami-Dade Development Site for $380M
stories.excerpt: Waste Management has paid nearly $380 million for about 146 acres in Medley, Fla., where the Houston-based company will likely build another landfill, property records show. The land sits parallel to Route 27 at 9515 Northwest 95th Avenue near the Everglades national park. About half the site remains vacant while the rest serves as a surface truck parking lot. The property sits adjacent to Waste Management’s 170-acre Medley Landfill complex. An entity tied to Hialeah Gardens-based Lowell Dunn Company sold the land. The same entity provided $366.8 million in seller financing, which is scheduled to mature in 2046. In a recorded easement, Lowell Dunn Company also agreed to allow Waste Management to install underground stormwater pipes across its neighboring property, enabling runoff from Waste Management’s site to discharge into a canal north of the property. Representatives for the buyer and seller did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The deal marks the second acquisition made by a waste management company in Miami-Dade County just this month. Woodlands, Texas-based Waste Connections paid $51 million for a 12-acre surface trucking parking lot in Miami Gardens. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Waste Management paid ~$380M for 146 acres in Medley, FL (Route 27, near Everglades).
Property half-vacant, half truck parking; adjacent to WM's 170-acre Medley Landfill complex.
Lowell Dunn Company provided $366.8M seller financing (maturity 2046); stormwater easement agreed.
stories.summary: Waste Management acquired approximately 146 acres in Medley, Florida, for nearly $380 million, where it plans to develop another landfill. The property, located at 9515 Northwest 95th Avenue near Route 27, sits adjacent to Waste Management's existing 170-acre Medley Landfill. Lowell Dunn Company financed $366.8 million of the purchase, with repayment scheduled for 2046.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. However, large-scale industrial/infrastructure investment in Miami-Dade County (Medley is west of Miami) indicates growth in waste management demand tied to population growth. Indirectly signals continued South Florida demographic expansion, which supports long-term multifamily demand in Miami, Broward, and Palm Beach metros, though landfill proximity may depress residential values in Medley proper.

stories.title: Carlyle Group, Haussmann Submit Plans for 99 Units at Brooklyn’s 566 Grand Avenue
stories.excerpt: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development have plans to partner on a 99-unit apartment complex in Brooklyn’s Crown Heights neighborhood. The two developers filed plans Thursday with the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) to bring a new 12-story mixed-use building to 566 Grand Avenue, near the corner of Grand Avenue and Bergen Street. Spokespeople for Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. If approved, the building will feature 99 Class A apartments, according to the filing, as well as ground-floor retail space. There will be 10 apartments on the second floor, 11 units each on the third through ninth floors, and four apartments each on floors 10, 11 and 12. The developers also plan to include several in-demand amenities at the property, such as a pet spa, a tenant theater, a game room, a children’s playroom, coworking space, a gym and an outdoor lounge. It is unclear if Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development plan to utilize the 485-x tax abatement program, which offers developers significant and lengthy tax breaks if their buildings feature a certain percentage of affordable housing. However, the 99-unit plan does provide a clue that this might be the case. A widely unpopular component of the 485-x program is higher construction wage requirements for buildings with 100 or more units. However, buildings with 99 or fewer units that utilize this program are not bound by those wage requirements. Crown Heights has been awash with residential building plans as of late. Avery Hall is planning an 18-story, 250-unit development at 1550 Bedford Avenue, while the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) is looking to build a 300-unit housing development in the neighborhood at 1119 Pacific Street. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development filed for 99-unit apartment at 566 Grand Ave, Brooklyn.
12-story Class A building in Crown Heights; ground-floor retail, full amenities (pet spa, theater, gym).
Planning filed with NYC DOB; potential 485-x tax abatement eligibility unclear.
stories.summary: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development filed plans with NYC's Department of Buildings for a 99-unit, 12-story Class A apartment building at 566 Grand Avenue in Brooklyn's Crown Heights neighborhood. The mixed-use development will feature ground-floor retail and extensive amenities including a pet spa, tenant theater, game room, and coworking space. The filing does not confirm 485-x tax abatement use.
stories.impact: Brooklyn Crown Heights continues to attract institutional capital and trophy development. This is market-rate Class A supply hitting a gentrifying/gentrified submarket. Watch whether Crown Heights rental absorb remains strong and rents justify $100k+ per-door development costs. If this project and others in the neighborhood are meeting absorption resistance, it may signal peak supply in that submarket and potential downside on future starts; conversely, quick pre-leasing would validate ongoing demand and encourage further capital inflow.

stories.title: Lightstone Capital Refis San Diego Apartments With $34M Loan

Located at 2700 Third Avenue, Kaya Apartments debuted last year with 78 units ranging from studios to two bedrooms. Community amenities at the fully-leased complex include coworking space, community lounge, a shared kitchen and on-site café. Located at 5010 Avenida Encinas 32 miles north of San Diego, the 98-unit apartment community with 15 designated as affordable housing will involve converting a former Studio 6 hotel. bullets: Lightstone Capital provided $34.25M bridge loan for Kaya Apartments, San Diego (78 units, Bankers Hill).
Newly completed, fully-leased asset; studios to 2-bed units; coworking, café, community lounge.
Developer Jeff Svitak; also closed $23.4M bridge for 98-unit TerraMar in Carlsbad, CA.
stories.summary: Lightstone Capital originated a $34.25 million senior bridge loan for Kaya Apartments, a 78-unit multifamily project developed by Jeff Svitak in San Diego's Bankers Hill neighborhood. The newly completed, fully-leased complex features studios to two-bedroom units and community amenities. Lightstone also closed a $23.4 million bridge for Alliance Development Services' 98-unit TerraMar project in Carlsbad.
stories.impact: Bridge financing activity for newly completed, stabilized assets signals refinance demand and potential cap-rate compression or difficulty securing permanent debt at developer expectations. San Diego's strong lease-up (Kaya fully leased at completion) indicates healthy demand, but bridge usage suggests either aggressive carry costs or forward-rate hedging. Monitor whether San Diego permanent financing tightens—early signal of capital constraints ahead of next-phase starts.

stories.title: Rexford Plans Up to $2B in Sales After Posting $507M Loss in Q2
stories.excerpt: Rexford Industrial Realty is dramatically accelerating its shift from being the most aggressive industrial buyer in Southern California into perhaps the region’s biggest seller. The Los Angeles-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has identified about $2 billion of “noncore assets” for disposition as it continues to prioritize keeping tenants in Rexford buildings. That property sales forecast is sharply up from the previous range of $400 million to $500 million. During the REIT’s earnings call Friday, CEO Laura Clark said the disposition pool encompasses about 8 million square feet with limited value-creation potential, shorter lease terms, and rents substantially above market — generally by more than 20 percent. Chief Financial Officer Michael Fitzmaurice said about $1 billion will repay debt maturing in 2027, rather than refinance into a higher rate environment. The remaining proceeds will be guided by market conditions. “We’re not de-levering to sit idle; we’re de-levering to redeploy,” Fitzmaurice said. The vast majority of Rexford’s property sales are expected to close before the end of the year. “We expect that pricing will be achieved at levels that allow us to redeploy proceeds on a neutral to accretive basis through our 2027 FFO per share, and this is not a dilutive exercise,” Clark said. Rexford said it sold seven properties totaling approximately 572,000 square feet for $137.9 million during the second quarter, after disposing of five properties for $127.4 million in the first quarter. The company previously known for 10-figure buying sprees has completed no acquisitions this year. Rexford plans to use property sales proceeds to repay debt, repurchase shares and pursue higher-yielding investments. It bought back $100 million of stock during the quarter, bringing its 2026 repurchases to $300 million, and its board subsequently authorized a new $1 billion repurchase program. The ramped-up disposition strategy also came with a $506.9 million
bullets: Rexford Industrial increased disposition target from $400–500M to ~$2B (8M SF noncore assets).
Q2 loss of $507M; rents 20%+ above market; CFO plans $1B debt paydown (2027 maturity).
CEO Clark: 'de-leveraging to redeploy,' signaling capital redeployment, not exit.
stories.summary: Rexford Industrial Realty dramatically expanded its disposition program from $400–500 million to approximately $2 billion of noncore assets (8 million square feet), following a $507 million loss in Q2. CEO Laura Clark cited rents substantially above market (>20%) and limited value-creation potential. CFO Michael Fitzmaurice said roughly $1 billion will repay debt maturing in 2027, with remaining proceeds guided by market conditions, positioning the firm to 'redeploy' capital.
stories.impact: Major Southern California industrial REIT forced into asset sales to manage debt maturity and above-market rents signals softening industrial demand and/or overbuilding in LA logistics. If Rexford—historically an aggressive buyer—is selling, it suggests diminished pricing power and higher vacancy in segments. While Rexford is industrial, not multifamily, significant distressed SoCal industrial selling could free capital and improve borrower balance sheets, freeing multifamily capital. However, broader signal: rising debt service costs (2027 maturity in higher-rate environment) compress returns across CRE. Watch for multifamily refinance walls in 2025–2026.

stories.title: Protective Live, Berkadia Provide $50M for Two Senior Living Facilities
stories.excerpt: Senior Living Transformation Company (SLTC) and Sabal Investment Holdings have secured $50 million to acquire and improve two senior living communities that specialize in assisted living and memory care: Daylesford Crossing in Paoli, Pa., and the Villages of Windcrest in Fredericksburg, Texas. Protective Life provided debt on the Villages of Windcrest, while Berkadia financed the Daylesford Crossing deal, according to a release. No broker was listed on the transaction. SLTC and Sabal plan numerous capital expenditures at the two assets, including improving the delivery of technology and operations, and will work with Juniper Communities, an established provider that will manage both facilities. “These acquisitions showcase SLTC’s and Sabal’s ability to provide solutions for challenged sellers within this critically important real estate sector,” said Arnie Whitman, founder and managing partner of SLTC. Located at 1450 East Lancaster Avenue in Paoli, a town 20 miles northwest of Downtown Philadelphia, Daylesford Crossing consists of 78 units. Located at 702 West Windcrest Street in Fredericksburg, a town 78 miles west of Austin, the Villages of Windcrest is 81 units. Tal Seder, managing director of Sabal Investment Holdings, described the two assets as “quality, well-located properties with upside potential” in a statement and referenced the demographic tailwinds from the baby boom generation that began turning 80 years old in 2026. “The combination of a sizable, aging baby boomer population and years of limited new construction is bringing the industry to an inflection point,” Seder said. “Investment in this sector is both critical and ripe with opportunity.” Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Protective Life and Berkadia provided $50M for two senior living acquisitions by SLTC/Sabal.
Daylesford Crossing (Paoli, PA, 20 mi NW of Philly); Villages of Windcrest (Fredericksburg, TX).
Capital deployed for tech/ops improvements; Juniper Communities to manage both properties.
stories.summary: Senior Living Transformation Company (SLTC) and Sabal Investment Holdings secured $50 million in financing from Protective Life and Berkadia to acquire and improve two senior living communities: Daylesford Crossing in Paoli, Pennsylvania (20 miles northwest of Philadelphia), and the Villages of Windcrest in Fredericksburg, Texas. The capital will fund technology and operations improvements, with Juniper Communities providing management.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Senior housing lending and value-add acquisition activity is a separate capital stream and asset class. However, continued provider financing and M&A in senior living (challenged-seller context) indicates sector stabilization post-COVID and demonstrates lender confidence in demographic (aging population) tailwinds—indirect affirmation of underlying demographic demand drivers relevant to mixed-age apartment markets.
